text: REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy with Direct Immunofluorescence. Do you notice any new blisters forming on your skin or mucous membranes, or has the existing rash remained stable since starting captopril?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology shows acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct Immunofluorescence reveals intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Blood tests confirm the presence of desmoglein antibodies. Clinical examination notes multiple flaccid blisters on the forearm (10% TBSA), positive Nikolsky sign, and ulcers on buccal, gingival, and vulvar mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy and antibody results confirm an autoimmune blistering condition affecting your skin and mucous membranes. Given the presence of desmoglein antibodies and the specific pattern of blisters and ulcers, I am ready to finalize your diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris.
